commits.message:
feat(ahand): replace silent auto-connect with step-by-step setup dialog

Replace the old useAHandAutoConnect hook with a Zustand-driven setup
dialog that shows 11 steps (5 aHand + 6 browser) with real-time status,
error messages, and per-step retry.

Key changes:
- Add useAHandSetupStore with step state machine and context passing
- Add AHandSetupDialog component with grouped step display
- Add Rust commands: start_daemon_only, browser_init_with_progress
- Rewrite LocalDeviceStatus as clickable summary that opens the dialog
- Wire auto-open on authenticated layout mount with daemon cleanup
- Strengthen browser_is_ready to check sockets dir and Node.js
- Fix retryFrom not to reset hasRun (avoids race with auto-trigger)
- Remove old useAHandAutoConnect, useBrowserInit, BrowserInitDialog
refactor(ui): move LocalDeviceStatus from sidebar to top bar

feat(desktop): add hidden DevTools toggle via avatar tap easter egg

Enable WebView DevTools in release builds by tapping the user avatar
10 times quickly in the profile popover, similar to Android's developer
mode activation.

feat(ahand): add activation steps to setup dialog with auto-accept mode

Add restart-daemon and verify-connection steps after browser setup,
set default_session_mode to auto_accept in generated config, and fix
browser step flow to continue to activation steps instead of breaking.

fix(ahand): improve daemon liveness check and strict device matching

- Use try_wait() in is_running() to detect exited/crashed daemon processes
- Require exact deviceId match for pairing approval, no fallback to any pending/approved device
- Retry reading device ID if not yet available instead of accepting wrong device
feat(build): add Apple signing credentials to desktop app build process

feat(build): add macOS code signing, notarization, and universal binary support

- Add Apple signing/notarization env vars to the build step
- Build universal binary (ARM64 + x86_64) with --target universal-apple-darwin
- Download both architectures of aHand daemon sidecar
- Install x86_64-apple-darwin Rust target for cross-compilation

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(build): pass --target directly to tauri CLI instead of through pnpm scripts

pnpm inserts an extra -- when forwarding args, causing --target to be
passed to cargo instead of tauri. Use pnpm -C to invoke tauri directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(build): create universal aHand binary with lipo for universal-apple-darwin target

Tauri expects a single universal binary for external binaries when building
with --target universal-apple-darwin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(build): produce arm64, x64, and universal macOS DMGs via matrix

Build three variants in parallel: aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin,
and universal-apple-darwin. Each gets the correct aHand sidecar binary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(reactions): normalize aggregated reactions from API to fix display after refresh

Backend returns aggregated reactions { emoji, count, userIds[] } but frontend
expected individual { userId, emoji } objects. After page refresh, reactions
showed wrong count and couldn't identify current user's reactions. Also added
user name display in reaction tooltips.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(client): add vitest infrastructure and reaction normalization tests

Set up vitest for the client app. Extract normalizeReactions to a
dedicated module and add 11 unit tests covering aggregated-to-individual
conversion, passthrough of WebSocket format, edge cases, and immutability.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(gitignore): add tmp directory to .gitignore
Merge branch 'main' into dev

feat(build): set app version from git tag during desktop build

Extract semver from the release tag and inject it into tauri.conf.json
before building, so the built app reflects the correct version number.
Also adds tasks module plan doc and updates lockfile.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(client): reset aHand setup state on workspace switch

aHand setup store was a global singleton with no workspace isolation.
Switching workspaces left stale appId/gatewayUrl/authToken from the
previous workspace, causing setup to skip or use wrong credentials.

- Add reset() action with generation counter to abort in-flight runs
- Reset aHand setup in MainSidebar workspace-switch effect
- Make useAHandStatus re-poll on workspace change (reset cached appId)
- Separate ahand_stop cleanup into unmount-only effect to avoid
  killing the daemon on workspace switches
Merge branch 'dev' of github.com:team9ai/team9 into dev

chore: add @sentry/cli to onlyBuiltDependencies

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(client): improve aHand setup error messages with specific diagnostics

Make every failure point in the device pairing flow transparent to users
by replacing generic error messages with detailed, context-aware diagnostics.

feat(client): add wait-for-bot step with countdown to aHand setup

Add a new "Wait for bot instance" step that polls the OpenClaw instance
status and listens for WebSocket user_online events, with a 150s countdown
timer displayed in the setup dialog UI.
Merge branch 'dev' of github.com:team9ai/team9 into dev

fix(client): improve aHand setup status handling with precise error messages

- find-app: switch on InstalledApplication.status (inactive/pending/error) instead of generic "not active" message
- wait-for-bot: check instance status (stopped/error) before entering countdown, fail fast instead of waiting 150s
- wait-for-bot: stop polling immediately on stopped/error status during countdown
- wait-for-bot: throw on any initial status check failure instead of silently proceeding

fix(client): augment PATH for macOS GUI and defer aHand setup until workspace ready

Add augmented_path() to include Homebrew, nvm, volta, fnm Node.js
paths that macOS GUI apps normally miss. Apply it to browser_init,
browser_is_ready, and browser_init_with_progress so ahandd can find
system Node.js reliably.

Improve browser-init failure messages with exit codes and step-specific
diagnostics instead of generic errors.

Defer aHand auto-start until selectedWorkspaceId is hydrated to prevent
403 errors from missing X-Tenant-Id header.

refactor(client): replace agent-browser with playwright-cli for browser automation

- Update browser_is_ready() to check for playwright-cli instead of agent-browser/daemon.js/sockets
- Simplify browser setup from 6 steps to 2 steps (Node.js + playwright-cli)
- Update BROWSER_STEP_MAP and error messages for new 2-step flow
- Remove browser-daemon, browser-socket, browser-chromium, browser-config steps from frontend store
- Enable headed mode by default in auto-generated config (visible browser window)
- Check both local (~/.ahand/node/bin/) and system PATH for playwright-cli

fix(client): capture ahandd stderr for accurate browser-init error reporting

- Pipe stderr from ahandd browser-init and read in separate thread to
  avoid deadlock while capturing actual error messages
- Use stderr (anyhow error) as error detail instead of stdout last line
  which was just a progress message
- Update browser_is_ready() comment to reflect self-contained install path

feat(db): add agent_task schema tables

Add 5 new tables for the tasks module:
- agent_task__tasks: main task table with lifecycle status
- agent_task__executions: execution records with TaskCast integration
- agent_task__steps: execution step tracking
- agent_task__deliverables: file deliverables per execution
- agent_task__interventions: human intervention requests

Includes enums, relations, indexes, and type exports.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(client): resolve Prism.js white screen caused by Vite chunk splitting

Vite's esbuild dep pre-bundling splits @lexical/code's Prism language
components into separate chunks with incorrect execution order —
prism-objectivec runs before prism-c it depends on, causing
"Cannot set properties of undefined" at Prism.languages.extend().

- Exclude @lexical/code from optimizeDeps to preserve ESM import order
- Centralize all Prism language imports in src/lib/prism.ts
- Update CodeBlock and MessageContent to use centralized import

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(server): prevent silent WebSocket broadcast failures for AI streaming messages

When agent-hive responded, the message was persisted to DB but intermittently
not delivered to clients via WebSocket. Root cause: a chain of silent failures
in the broadcast pipeline where Redis cache write errors cascaded to drop the
entire member lookup, and error swallowing in sendToChannelMembers hid the
failure from callers.

Fixes:
- channel-member-cache: Redis cache write is now best-effort (try-catch) so
  a non-critical cache failure no longer prevents member IDs from being returned
- websocket.gateway: sendToChannelMembers returns boolean success indicator
  instead of silently swallowing all errors

docs(spec): add Phase 1.5 onboarding integration to routine creation spec

The existing workspace onboarding flow has a design gap: users select task
titles during onboarding (e.g. "Daily team digest"), but these choices are
persisted as plain strings in tenant.settings.onboarding.tasks.selectedTaskTitles
and only used later as prompt context for agent generation. They never become
actionable — users who completed onboarding had no way to turn "the tasks I
said I want" into "the routines I actually run".

The draft status added by Phase 1 is the exact primitive needed to fix this.
Phase 1.5 has the onboarding provisioning pipeline create a draft routine per
selected task (and per customTask), assigned to the user's personal-staff bot.
The user arrives at the Routine list with N drafts ready for "Complete
Creation" — each refined via the same agentic conversation flow from Phase 1.

Changes to the spec:

- New data model field: routine__routines.source_ref (nullable varchar,
  indexed). Format: onboarding:{workspaceOnboardingId}:{onboardingTaskId}.
  Makes re-provisioning idempotent without needing a separate mapping table.

- New RoutinesService.create signature: optional 4th argument
  options?: { sourceRef?: string } for internal callers (not exposed in HTTP
  DTO — external API consumers don't know about onboarding's internal IDs).

- New service method: OnboardingService.provisionRoutines(). Iterates the
  user's selected tasks + customTask, idempotently creates drafts via
  RoutinesService.create(..., { sourceRef }). Wired into the existing
  provisionOnboardingResources pipeline after provisionCommonStaff and before
  persistPreferences. Full pseudocode included in the spec.

- persistPreferences updated: drop selectedTaskTitles from
  tenant.settings.onboarding.tasks. The draft routines themselves become the
  canonical representation of user intent. selectedTaskIds and customTask
  strings remain for audit/debug.

- Grep-and-replace work item: any existing code that reads selectedTaskTitles
  for prompt context must be updated to query routine__routines WHERE
  source_ref LIKE 'onboarding:%' AND creator_id = userId instead.

- Updated Scope, Implementation Sequence (added tasks 13-18 for Phase 1.5),
  and Overview (now mentions 3 creation paths instead of 2).

- Edge cases documented: missing personal-staff bot, skipped onboarding,
  re-provisioning idempotency, user deletes a provisioned draft.

- Phase 1.5 implementation depends on Phase 1 tasks 1 (schema) and 3
  (RoutinesService.create accepting options.sourceRef), so it can be
  executed right after Phase 1 in the same sprint.

Rev 3 in the spec Changelog. Rev 2 (earlier today) fixed the original
architectural mistakes; Rev 3 expands scope to include onboarding as the
first large-scale draft producer.

fix(channels): prevent orphan echo channels with atomic create + self-heal

The self-chat ("echo") creation path was non-atomic and used a member-join
existence check, so a failing addMember left an orphan channel row that no
subsequent call could ever find or reuse. Every retry inserted a fresh
orphan and surfaced "Failed to create echo channel" to the user.

(type, created_by, tenant_id), repair orphans in place via a new
ensureEchoOwnerMembership helper, and create fresh channel + owner rows
inside a single db.transaction. Post-commit cache invalidation stays
outside the transaction. The orphan-heal INSERT uses onConflictDoNothing
to stay safe under a concurrent self-heal race.

fix(views): drop seq_id from view message response to avoid BigInt crash

TableView (and any Table/Board/Calendar view) was returning HTTP 500 with
"Do not know how to serialize a BigInt" because ViewsService.queryMessages
spread the raw Drizzle row into the response via `...m`. The im_messages
schema declares seq_id as bigint in BigInt mode, so the spread dragged a JS
BigInt into the payload, which Express's JSON.stringify cannot handle.

Chat view's list messages endpoint was unaffected because it maps rows to
MessageResponse explicitly and never carries seq_id. Views used the raw
$inferSelect row, so the leak was view-specific.

Fix: introduce a private serializeMessageForView helper that destructures
seq_id out of the message row (the client's ViewMessageItem type doesn't
consume it anyway) and tacks the property map on. All three response paths
in queryMessages — flat pagination, grouped with specific group, grouped
with all groups — now go through the helper, so no future spread can
re-introduce the leak.

fix(routines): address Codex Round 2 review findings

Codex Round 2 surfaced 5 issues (1 critical blocker + 4 important) that
previous review rounds missed. Fixed 4, documented 1 as a known edge case.

Critical: im-worker post-broadcast fanout for routine-session
-------------------------------------------------------------
Phase 1 im-worker only auto-forwarded chat replies to the bot when
channel.type was 'direct' or 'tracking'. The new 'routine-session' type
was treated as a group channel, meaning the initial kickoff event worked
but every subsequent user reply in the creation channel was dropped
(without @mention) or routed into a fresh tracking session (with
@mention) — the creation conversation was fundamentally broken after
turn 1.

- post-broadcast.service.ts: add `isRoutineSession` check alongside
  `isDm`; set `alwaysForward=true`; map session scope to `dm/{channelId}`
  so follow-up messages land on the same session the gateway's kickoff
  event used; skip tracking-channel creation; report 'dm' location type;
  treat as dm-like in deriveTeam9Context (but NOT as isMentorDm — that
  flag only fires for real direct channels).
- Suppress notification tasks for routine-session channels (user doesn't
  need "new message" alerts for their own creation chat).
- New tests: routes routine-session to dm/ scope + forwards without
  @mention + does not create a tracking channel.

Important: RoutineList stuck in creation mode after completeCreation
--------------------------------------------------------------------
`isCreationMode` was derived from local `selectedRun` alone, so ChatArea
kept showing the yellow "In Creation" banner after the routine
transitioned from draft to upcoming, leaving users stuck viewing an
archived creation channel. Added a status guard plus a useEffect that
clears the creation selection when `selectedRoutine.status !== 'draft'`.

Important: deleted draft detail keeps polling
----------------------------------------------
DraftRoutineCard's delete mutation only invalidated `['routines']`.
`RoutineList.activeRoutineId` and `selectedRun` stayed set, and the
`['routine', id]` detail query kept polling a now-deleted row.

- DraftRoutineCard: accept new `onDeleted?: (routineId: string) => void`
  prop; in delete mutation onSuccess, removeQueries for the detail key
  and invoke onDeleted so the parent can reset state.
- RoutineList: new `handleDraftDeleted` callback that collapses the
  routine's expanded state and clears activeRoutineId/selectedRun when
  the deleted routine was the active one.
- DraftRoutineCard test: add coverage for the delete success path
  including removeQueries call.

Important: atomic claim can't heal half-populated drafts
--------------------------------------------------------
The Round 1 atomic-claim UPDATE used
  `WHERE creation_channel_id IS NULL AND creation_session_id IS NULL`
which could never match a legacy row with (channel_id null,
session_id set) left behind by older rollback bugs. Dropped the
session_id predicate: the claim now matches on `creation_channel_id
IS NULL` only, overwriting any stale session_id as it heals the row.
Still race-safe because optimistic locking only needs one atomic column.

Deferred: race loser returns ids before winner's kickoff commits
----------------------------------------------------------------
In the extremely narrow window where two concurrent callers race AND
the winner's sendInput() then fails, the race loser can return the
winner's ids to its caller before the winner's rollback clears them.
Documented as a known limitation in a code comment at the race-loser
return site. A proper fix requires either a pg advisory lock held
across the network call or an `is_ready` marker column — both are
out-of-scope for P0. User retry reliably recovers.

fix(bot-auth): propagate tenantId from bot token + add L1 memory cache

Bot requests via internal Railway DNS hit TenantMiddleware's host-based
tenant resolution, which never matches — leaving `req.tenantId` undefined.
`routine-bot.service.getRoutineOrThrow` then passed undefined to drizzle
`eq(tenantId, undefined)`, and postgres-js throws `UNDEFINED_VALUE`,
surfacing as a 500 with no useful stack in logs (OtelLogger coerced the
raw Error object into `[object Object]` because BaseExceptionFilter
passes the exception positionally).

AuthGuard now pulls tenantId out of the bot token via
`validateAccessTokenWithContext` and writes it to `request.tenantId`
(without overwriting a pre-set middleware value). The cache path adds
an in-memory L1 tier in front of Redis — short TTL (5s positive /
1s negative) bounds staleness across multi-instance deploys while
eliminating network round-trips on hot paths; invalidateBot and
beginBotMutation evict the bot's local entries.

CustomSentryFilter now logs `message + stack` as separate args so
OtelLogger produces a readable body.

feat(staff-bootstrap): persist user locale + inject into bootstrap events

Add end-to-end plumbing so `team9:bootstrap.start` events carry the
mentor's preferred language (BCP 47) and IANA time zone, which
`team9-staff-bootstrap` reads from `team9Context` to greet the user in
the right language and format times in their local zone. Wave 1 (in
`team9-agent-pi`) wired the agent-side consumption; this commit is
the gateway + client + DB half of the flow.

## Schema

- `im_users` gets two new nullable columns, `language` (varchar(16)) and
  `time_zone` (varchar(64)). Manual migration 0042 following the
  existing numbered-ALTER-TABLE pattern — pre-existing snapshot
  collisions in `meta/` prevent `drizzle-kit generate` from working
  cleanly, so this follows the same approach used by 0036–0041.

- `Team9SessionContext` (agent-pi side) already has `language?` and
  `timeZone?` fields from Wave 1, so no type change is needed — the
  gateway just starts populating them.

## Gateway

- `UpdateUserDto` accepts `language` + `timeZone` with conservative
  regex validation: BCP 47 2/3-letter primary subtag with optional
  4–8-char subsequent subtags, and IANA `zone(/zone)*` of
  letters/digits/`+-_`. Matches real tags ("zh-CN", "pt-BR",
  "sr-Cyrl-RS", "Asia/Shanghai", "America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires",
  "Etc/GMT+8") without being permissive enough to accept arbitrary
  strings.

- `UsersService` plumbs the two new fields through `findById`,
  `getMultipleByIds`, search, and `mapUserResponse`. `agentType`
  stays at the end of the mapped response to keep the Redis-cached
  JSON key order stable for the existing cache-read test.

- `AuthService.serializeAuthenticatedUser` / `AuthenticatedUserResponse`
  now carry `language` + `timeZone` so `/api/v1/auth/me` exposes them
  to the client on login and on session restore.

- `PersonalStaffService.createStaff` and `CommonStaffService.createStaff`
  each grow a tiny private `getUserLocale(userId)` helper that reads
  the two columns from `im_users`, and spread them into the
  `team9Context` payload — but ONLY when non-null — so the agent-side
  "unknown language → English default" branch keeps kicking in cleanly
  for users who haven't reported preferences yet.

- `PERSONAL_STAFF_JOB_DESCRIPTION` constant changes from the generic
  "Personal AI assistant" to "Dedicated personal assistant for your
  owner". This is the string the agent sees when it fetches its own
  profile, and the bootstrap prompt on the agent side frames the
  relationship as one-to-one. "Personal AI assistant" was too generic
  to support that framing.

## Client

- `User` type and `imApi.updateMe` signature accept `language` +
  `timeZone`.

- New `useSyncUserLocale` hook: on authenticated bootstrap, detect the
  browser's current `i18n.language` and
  `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, compare with the
  persisted values on the current user, and PATCH only the fields
  that differ. Fire-and-forget — failure is non-fatal and the next
  bootstrap retries. Uses a `useRef` guard so StrictMode double-invoke
  and subsequent re-renders do not flood the server with duplicate
  PATCHes.

- `_authenticated.tsx` layout calls the hook alongside the existing
  WebSocket / heartbeat / service-worker bootstrap. This is the single
  place that runs both on fresh login and on session restore from
  localStorage, so one call site covers both entry paths.

## Tests

- `users.service.spec` — 17 new assertions: three update-tests for
  language-only / timeZone-only / both persistence, plus parametrised
  DTO validation for BCP 47 and IANA regex accept/reject cases.

- `personal-staff.service.spec` — language/timeZone included in
  bootstrap payload when set, omitted when unset. The existing
  jobDescription assertion is updated to the new constant value.

- `personal-staff.controller.spec` — `makeGetStaffResult` fixture

- `common-staff.service.spec` — same two bootstrap tests via

  locale-shaped row through it is fragile).

- `useSyncUserLocale.test.tsx` — 6 new Vitest hook tests covering:
  no-op when user is still null, PATCH with both fields on fresh
  user, partial PATCH when only one side differs, no PATCH when both

fix(bot-auth): address multi-round review of L1 cache correctness

Iterative Codex-driven review of the prior commit (1be188fa) surfaced a
Critical tenant-crossing vulnerability plus several Important L1 cache
correctness gaps. Rather than piecemeal fixes, reworked the cache to
guarantee cross-node correctness under rotation, reconnect, and in-flight
request races.

Critical
- Bot branch of AuthGuard now UNCONDITIONALLY overrides request.tenantId
  from the bot token. Previously the "don't overwrite middleware value"
  check let an attacker-forged X-Tenant-ID header re-scope a bot request
  into another tenant. The bot's installed-application tenantId is the
  only authoritative source for a bot-authenticated request.

Important — L1 cross-node consistency
- Added Redis pub/sub invalidation. BotAuthCacheService subscribes to
  bot-auth:invalidate via a dedicated ioredis duplicate connection on
  onModuleInit; invalidateBot / beginBotMutation publish the botId after
  their Redis state changes. Subscribers evict their local L1 entries
  for the bot. Adds publish() + createSubscriber() to @team9/redis.
- ready-event handler is attached ONLY AFTER the initial subscribe
  succeeds — a failed initial subscribe tears down the subscriber and
  disables L1 entirely, so a later reconnect cannot silently re-enable
  L1 without ever having subscribed to the channel.

Important — in-flight write races
- Replaced the time-based invalidate epoch with a monotonic (era, seq)
  pair that is stamped by every invalidate and captured at every
  request start. writeMemory rejects any positive whose startEra is
  older than current (subscriber disconnect/reconnect window) or whose
  startSeq precedes an invalidateSeq for the same bot (mid-load race).
  The guard has no time component, so even a multi-second in-flight
  request cannot repopulate stale L1 after pruning.

Important — same-node mutation window
- Added localMutationRefCounts (refcounted) that writeMemory consults:
  while a bot is mid-begin/end mutation locally, L1 promotion is
  refused regardless of seq, closing the gap between recordInvalidation
  and the awaited Redis mutation-flag write. Refcounted so overlapping
  same-bot mutations compose correctly.

Important — inflight promise sharing
- The inflight dedupe map now stores {promise, startEra, startSeq} with
  the ORIGINAL creator's captures. A second caller that shares the
  promise validates the result against those captures (not its own),
  so an invalidation landing between the promise's creation and the
  shared-consumer's arrival correctly marks the result stale for the
  consumer — which falls through to a fresh loader instead of silently
  returning the pre-invalidation value.

Important — fail-closed cache path
- isBotMutationInProgress now takes an onError option. Cache-serving
  path (getValidCachedContext) opts into 'closed' so a Redis blip
  during a rotation cannot leak the cached positive. Loader path in
  bot.service.findValidatedAccessTokenMatch keeps the default
  'open' — the DB is still authoritative there and failing closed
  would DoS all auth on any Redis blip.

Important — skip L1 when version read fails
- writeMemory is now inside the versioned.version !== null block of the
  loader path. Previously L1 got promoted even when the Redis-layer
  positive write was skipped for version-read failure, leaving an
  unfenced L1 entry.

Important — cache shape migration
- cacheKey prefix bumped to auth:bot-token:v2: so the old
  {botId,userId,tenantId}-only payload (without email/username) is
  never read back. Defense in depth: getValidCachedContext also
  rejects and deletes any cached context missing those string fields.

Important — logging
- CustomSentryFilter now logs an explicit message+stack via Logger.error
  so OtelLogger produces a readable body. Previously the raw Error
  object was passed positionally and serialized as "[object Object]",
  making 500 root-cause invisible in Railway logs.

Runtime resilience
- Subscriber error / close / end events call disableL1 (memoryCache +
  byBotId cleared, l1CrossNodeReady=false); ready event calls
  enableL1AfterSubscribe which bumps l1Era and clears maps so no
  pre-outage L1 entry can survive reconnect. invalidateSeqs is
  preserved across reconnect — the era guard handles outage-straddling
  requests separately.

Tests — 38 cases in bot-auth-cache.service.spec.ts
- New coverage: L1 hit/miss/TTL/size cap, pub/sub local+remote, subscribe
  reject teardown, subscribe-rejected-no-ready-handler, ready-on-close
  reconnect recovery, mid-load seq race, pre-outage era race, long-lived
  in-flight (no prune), same-node begin/end race, overlapping same-bot
  mutations (refcount), inflight promise stale-for-second-caller,
  transient mutation-in-progress not promoted, negative entries stay

fix(common-staff): prevent truncated persona on 3-candidate generation

The 三选一 candidate generation flow streams three distinct personas
through Vercel AI SDK's structured-output mode. Claude (via OpenRouter)
defaults `max_tokens` to roughly 1024, which is not enough for three
~300-word personas plus JSON structural overhead. When the budget runs
out mid-stream, Vercel AI SDK resolves `result.output` with the partial
object — the last candidate's persona is cut off mid-sentence — and
`finishReason` is `"length"`. Nothing in the old pipeline distinguished
this from a clean completion, so the truncated object flowed through
to the frontend and the user could pick and save a half-written
persona.

Fix is four-part, all of it in this commit:

- `staff.service.ts` sets `maxOutputTokens: 4096` explicitly on the
  `streamText` call (comfortable headroom for three full personas +
  JSON), and awaits `result.finishReason` after the stream drains.
  If `finishReason === 'length'`, throw a clear error naming the cap
  so the async generator fails loudly instead of yielding a
  `complete` event with a truncated object.

- `common-staff.service.spec.ts` gets a regression test that drives
  the mocked `streamText` with `finishReason: 'length'` and asserts
  the generator rejects with a `/max_tokens limit/` error. The
  pre-existing prompt-assembly test also gains a `maxOutputTokens:
  4096` check so nobody silently removes the cap later. To support
  both, `mockStreamTextWithOutputReturn` now accepts an optional
  `finishReason` parameter defaulting to `'stop'` so existing
  happy-path tests stay unchanged.

- `applications.ts` (client) — the SSE parser used to only handle
  `[DONE]` and `{type, data}` events and silently ignored anything
  else, which means the server-side error event (emitted when the
  async generator throws) was swallowed. Now the parser explicitly
  detects an `{error: "..."}` payload and throws it, letting the
  dialog's catch block react.

- `CreateCommonStaffDialog.tsx` — the catch block now clears
  `candidates` and `selectedCandidate` before setting the error
  state. Without this, the dialog still displayed whichever partial
  candidates had streamed before the error and let the user click
  through to save them — exactly the truncation bug.

Together these four changes close the loop: the server throws on
`length`, the error propagates over SSE, the client parser re-throws
it, and the dialog clears partial UI state so the user cannot save a
truncated persona. The `maxOutputTokens` bump alone probably prevents
the symptom in practice, but the defensive plumbing around it is what
keeps the next provider / model change from silently reintroducing
the bug.

fix(routines): allow multiple concurrent drafts per (user, bot)

The agentic routine-creation flow (`POST /v1/routines/with-creation-task`)
used to 400 with "You already have a draft routine being created with
this agent. Complete or delete it first." as soon as the user had ANY
in-progress draft against the same bot. Two problems with that rule:

1. **Semantically wrong.** Drafts are a first-class entity. A real user
   plausibly wants to be building several different routines with the
   same personal assistant at the same time — e.g. "weekly sales report"
   and "daily standup summary" both belong to the same assistant but
   are obviously distinct tasks. Forcing them to be serialized is
   artificial.

2. **One-way trap.** A single stuck draft (claw-hive transiently down,
   user closing the browser mid-bootstrap, a server-side rollback
   leaving the row orphaned, the fresh `staffKind` migration landing
   before someone retries) blocks ALL subsequent creations against that
   bot with no in-UI recovery path. The reporter ran into exactly this:
   four stale drafts accumulated from earlier test data, and the UI
   just showed "Request failed with status 400" with no way to know
   that unrelated historical drafts were the cause.

Remove the pre-flight SELECT in `createWithCreationTask`. The flow now:

  - Always creates a new draft row + new creation session channel.
  - Leaves existing drafts untouched.
  - Relies on the frontend to disable the trigger button while the
    request is pending (already handled) and on the drafts-list UI to
    surface existing drafts so the user can pick one up if they want.

If accidental double-creation becomes a real problem in the future, the
right place to fix it is the client (debounce) and the drafts-list UI
(make existing drafts obvious and resumable), not a server-side 400
that silently blocks the happy path.

Test updates:

- `routines.service.spec.ts` — drop the "already have a draft" test and
  replace it with a regression guard that drives `setupHappyPath` and
  asserts a SECOND `createWithCreationTask` call actually creates a new
  draft + channel + kickoff event (no short-circuit). The comment above
  the test documents the pathology and asks whoever reintroduces the
  check to first read this changelog. `setupHappyPath` itself drops
  the draft-conflict mock (step 4).

- `routines-creation-flow.integration.spec.ts` — same mock-queue cleanup:
  the `db.limit.mockResolvedValueOnce([])` that was seeding an empty
  draft-conflict response is gone, and a short comment marks the
  removal for the next reader.

fix(client): guard self-sync against auth-swap and store-user-change races

The user_updated handler fires getCurrentUser() as a floating promise
and pushed the result into the Zustand app store unconditionally. If
the request is still in flight when the user logs out and a different
user logs in (or when the auth token otherwise swaps), the late
response could overwrite the new user's state with stale data from
the previous session.

At promise-resolution time, re-verify that
(a) the fetched user id matches the event we reacted to, and
(b) it still matches the currently logged-in user read from the
    authoritative Zustand store (not the effect closure, which is
    stale across an identity swap).
Drop the sync if either guard fails.

fix(tracking): keep Started first; surface thinking row from stream start

Two related fixes to the live thinking UX:

1. Clamp effective time in `sortByEffectiveTime` so thinking can never
   sort above its round's agent_start. The LLM call can begin a few ms
   before the tracking observer finishes persisting `agent_start`, so
   `thinking.startedAt` legitimately predates `agent_start.createdAt` —
   the previous unbounded sort then flipped the rows to "Thought for X
   / Started", reading as if thinking happened *before* the round
   began. The clamp treats the latest preceding agent_start as a
   floor, keeping lifecycle markers as round boundaries.

2. Show `StreamingThinkingRow` from the moment the stream starts
   instead of gating on `stream.isThinking || stream.thinking.length`.
   Claude only flushes thinking deltas when a reasoning block
   finalizes, so during the first several seconds the store has
   `thinking === ""` — the previous condition kept the row hidden
   for the entire "obviously thinking" interval. The row now has two
   phases: pulsing "Thinking Ns" while `stream.content` is empty,
   then freezes to "Thought for Ns" (frozen duration, no pulse) once
   reply text arrives. Bots that reply without any thinking get the
   row hidden entirely once content starts, so no false
   "Thought for 0s" remnant.

fix(tracking): freeze StreamingThinkingRow duration on first content

Without freezing, the "Thought for Ns" label in the live streaming
row kept climbing through the entire reply-streaming phase. Cause:
`durationMs` was computed as `Date.now() - stream.startedAt` inside
the component body, so every text-delta re-render re-read the clock.
The counter visibly "stopped" only when the stream ended and the
persisted thinking row took over — users saw the label tick several
seconds past where it should have frozen.

Fix: capture the elapsed duration into a `useRef` the first render
`hasContent` flips true, and read from the ref on subsequent
renders. Paired with agent-pi #48 (which reports the same thinking
span for the persisted row), the streaming→persisted handoff now
stays at a stable number.

Regression test: fake timers, rerender twice (t+4s with content,
t+14s with more content), assert the label reads "Thought for 4s"
both times, not "Thought for 14s". Verified as a true guard —
reverting the useRef fix makes the test go red.

fix(onboarding): close race conditions in createRecord and complete() (#42)

* fix(onboarding): close race conditions in createRecord and complete()

createRecord used check-then-insert, so two concurrent callers (duplicate
webhook, double tab) could both pass the findRecord guard and collide on
the (tenant_id, user_id) unique index. Replaced with
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING, falling back to findRecord
when the duplicate caller loses.

complete() read status, checked guards, then did an unconditional
UPDATE SET status='provisioning' — TOCTOU window let two concurrent
callers both start provisioning and create duplicate routines/channels/
staff. Replaced with a compare-and-swap: UPDATE ... SET status=
'provisioning', version = version + 1 WHERE id = X AND status IN
('completed','failed') RETURNING. Losers re-read to emit a precise error

fix(im): route topic-session wire payload as 'dm' to match agent-pi's EventChannelType

Root cause of the "agent doesn't reply" bug observed during local
testing: the topic-session wire payload used location.type='topic',
session-id scope='topic', and team9Context.scopeType='topic'. But
agent-pi's EventChannelType is a closed 4-value enum
('channel' | 'dm' | 'task' | 'tracking'), and its Team9Component
.updateEventLocationFromLocation switch handles exactly those 4
values — 'topic' falls through to the `else` branch, leaves
channelType undefined, and the DM-specific prompt injection + plain-
text streaming path never kicks in. Agent-produced text ends up in
the "regular channel" path where it's swallowed unless a Reply tool
is called, so the user sees silence.

Fix follows agent-pi's existing dispatch pattern:

- team9 IM channel types that behave one-on-one at the agent runtime
  layer (direct, routine-session, and now topic-session) all map to
  the 'dm' wire scope. They share location.type='dm', session id
  scope='dm', and team9Context.scopeType='dm'. channelId is UUIDv7-
  unique so there is no id collision across the three sub-types.
- team9 IM distinctions continue to live on channels.type (sidebar
  grouping, search, title generation all key off 'topic-session').
  The mapping to 'dm' only happens at the wire, so no bounded-
  context leak into agent-pi runtime.
- Identical to the way routine-session has always been routed
  (location.type='dm', scope='dm', scopeType='dm'). Grep for
  'routine-session' in agent-pi's claw-hive package returns zero
  channelType-level references for exactly this reason.

An earlier attempt added 'topic' as a fifth EventChannelType
literal on agent-pi. That path required touching 13 distinct call
sites across component.ts, message-xml.ts, and tools.ts, leaked the
team9 IM concept into agent-pi's runtime contract, and would have
repeated the same 13-site change for every future "DM-like" channel
type. The mapping approach matches the existing routine-session
pattern and keeps the wire contract closed at four values.

- post-broadcast.service.ts: location.type, session-id scope, and
  deriveTeam9Context.scopeType all produce 'dm' for topic-session
  (three hunks + comment rewrite).
- topic-sessions.service.ts: buildSessionId uses /dm/, createSession
  sends team9Context.scopeType='dm', stale JSDoc fixed.

fix(im): route topic-session title LLM through capability-hub; fix grouped tenantId filter

Two bugs surfaced while investigating "title never shows up":

### Bug 1 — Title LLM bypassed capability-hub / billing

TopicTitleGeneratorService was calling @team9/ai-client's ClaudeProvider,
which reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env and hits api.anthropic.com
directly. That path bypasses capability-hub's pre-authorize → record →
billing-hub pipeline — i.e. every title generation would have been an
unbilled platform-key LLM call, mixing platform cost into a feature
that should be charged to the workspace like any other LLM call. It
also meant local dev with a placeholder ANTHROPIC_API_KEY silently
401'd every call and swallowed the title.

Changed the generator to proxy through capability-hub's llm-proxy:

- Dependency swap: AiClientService → CapabilityHubClient (exported by
  DeepResearchModule, which TopicSessionsModule now imports).
- callLlm() does `POST ${CAPABILITY_HUB_URL}/proxy/openrouter/chat/completions`
  with `serviceHeaders({ userId, tenantId })` so capability-hub can

### Bug 2 — listGrouped tenantId filter wrong in community edition

In community edition the @CurrentTenantId() decorator returns
undefined when TenantMiddleware can't resolve a tenant from the
request (e.g. no X-Tenant-Id header + localhost host with no
"default" tenant row). listGrouped / listLegacyDirectOnly's filter
was `tenantId ? eq(...) : isNull(channels.tenantId)` — so an
undefined tenantId forced `channels.tenantId IS NULL`, which excludes
every tenanted channel (i.e. every topic session).

Replaced both occurrences with `tenantId ? eq(...) : undefined`,
matching the codebase convention used in channels.service.ts and
everywhere else — undefined is dropped by drizzle's and() and simply
doesn't filter.

* fix(onboarding): close race conditions in createRecord and complete()

createRecord used check-then-insert, so two concurrent callers (duplicate
webhook, double tab) could both pass the findRecord guard and collide on
the (tenant_id, user_id) unique index. Replaced with

(or return the winning row if the race winner already finished).
Subsequent provisioning now reads from the CAS RETURNING row rather than
the pre-CAS snapshot to avoid acting on stale stepData. Terminal
provisioned/failed writes also bump version for monotonicity.

provisioned short-circuits, CAS-lost-to-provisioning, CAS-lost-to-

* feat(gateway/ahand): hub->gateway webhook receiver + events gateway stub

POST /api/ahand/hub-webhook ingests device events from ahand-hub.
Auth is HMAC-SHA256 (no JWT), verified over the raw request body
(express.raw() registered before json() in main.ts for this path).
5-minute timestamp freshness window defends against replay.

Idempotency: Redis SETNX ahand:webhook:seen:{eventId} / 600s TTL.
On handler failure the key is cleared before re-throwing so the hub's
retry actually re-attempts the work.

Event handlers:
  device.online     set presence key + update last_seen_at
  device.heartbeat  refresh presence TTL only (no DB write)
  device.offline    del presence key + update last_seen_at
  device.revoked    del presence key + flip DB status=revoked
  device.registered fan-out only (DB row created during registration)

Fan-out: AhandRedisPublisher (cross-replica im-worker delivery) +
AhandEventsGateway stub (Socket.io; Task 4.7 wires the server ref).
Unknown deviceIds are logged and skipped -- no throw.

AhandEventsGateway is a simple @Injectable exposing emitToOwner().

fix(gateway/ahand): use NestFactory rawBody option instead of path-scoped raw() (#61)

The path-scoped \`raw({type: 'application/json'})\` middleware replaced
req.body with a Buffer, which then fed into NestJS ValidationPipe and
crashed with \`TypeError: Cannot delete property '0' of [object
Uint8Array]\` when \`whitelist: true\` tried to strip extra keys from
what it thought was an object.

Switch to NestFactory({rawBody: true}), which has the platform adapter
stash the raw Buffer on req.rawBody AND still parse req.body as JSON.
The webhook controller already prefers req.rawBody when available:

  const raw = (req as ... ).rawBody ?? req.body;
  ...
  @Body() body: WebhookEventDto

Result: HMAC verifier gets the exact byte sequence the hub signed, and
ValidationPipe gets a proper DTO to validate.

Also drop the unused \`raw\` import from express.

still produced an unusable request body shape for the controller.

fix(gateway/ahand): stash rawBody via json() verify callback (#62)

fix(im-worker/ahand): disable readyCheck on subscriber duplicate (#63)

The subscriber's duplicated ioredis client inherited enableReadyCheck:
true, which issues INFO on every (re)connect. Once psubscribe puts the
connection into SUBSCRIBE mode, Redis rejects the INFO probe with
'Connection in subscriber mode, only subscriber commands may be used'.
The error fires on the 'error' handler → ioredis marks the connection
bad → triggers reconnect → same INFO fails → infinite loop. Messages
never delivered to pmessage handler.

Fix: pass {enableReadyCheck: false} to redis.duplicate(). Subscriptions
don't need readyCheck since psubscribe itself fails if the connection
isn't usable.

* fix(wiki): re-seed DocumentEditor on server commit and async draft arrival

DocumentEditor's InitialContentPlugin ingests `initialContent` exactly
once per mount, so updating `body` in React state after mount was a
no-op in the Lexical editor. Two real-world paths hit this: (a) a
server commit arriving while the user is viewing a clean page, and
(b) `useWikiDraft` loading a draft asynchronously from localStorage
after mount.

Drive a `key` on `DocumentEditor` that bumps on explicit re-seed
events only — never on keystrokes — so the editor remounts with
fresh `initialContent` when the server refreshes (while clean) or
when a draft first arrives. User typing produces new draft object
identities via `setDraft`, but a `draftSeededRef` gate ensures the
editor stays mounted across those re-deliveries so the Lexical
cursor and focus are preserved. Initial-mount refs skip the first
effect run to avoid a spurious remount on the already-seeded
`useState` initializers.

* fix(wiki): harden validateWikiPath - empty segments + reserve leading "-"

Two related additions to the wiki-path validator, both touching the
same per-segment loop so they land together:

Fix B-3: reject empty segments (`foo//bar`, `foo/`, doubled/trailing
slashes). The previous all-dots regex `seg.length > 0 && /^\.+$/.test(seg)`
let an empty segment slip through as "allowed" because the length check
was vestigial. Rejecting up-front is simpler than trusting folder9's
`filepath.Clean` to collapse consistently, and closes the tiny gap
where a malformed path could bypass the rest of the segment checks.
The new rule is ordered BEFORE the all-dots check so the regex never
receives an empty string.

New rule (support for B-6): the FIRST segment must not start with `-`.
This is a permanent reservation so route prefixes like
`/wiki/:slug/-/review` can never collide with a user-authored path
when B-6 restructures the routes. Only the top-level segment is gated
— nested files/dirs starting with `-` (e.g. `foo/-bar.md`) stay
allowed, and `review-plan.md` at the top level is still fine (only a
LITERAL leading `-` is banned).

Tests:
  - 3 empty-segment rejects (`foo//bar.md`, `foo/`, `/`)
  - 2 leading-`-` rejects (`-review/anything.md`, `-foo`)
  - 1 leading-`-` accept for nested (`foo/-bar.md`)
  - 1 accept for `review-plan.md` (literal `-` not at start)
Removed the 2 pre-existing "allows empty segment" edge-case tests since
those cases are now rejections.

* fix(wiki): raise icon max length to 32 for ZWJ emoji

fail validation it just passed.

perf(im-worker): dedupe getMessageWithContext between webhook + hive fan-out (#76)

`PostBroadcastService.processTask` dispatches `pushToBotWebhooks` and
`pushToHiveBots` concurrently via Promise.all. Each previously fired its
own `getMessageWithContext` call — 8-10 redundant DB roundtrips per
message in any channel that had both webhook and hive bots.

Both helpers now accept an optional `MessageContextLoader` callback.
processTask creates a per-call lazy memoized loader: the first
dereference triggers the underlying query, the second returns the
already-resolved promise. The callback is `undefined` for direct test
invocations (and falls back to `this.getMessageWithContext(msgId)`),
preserving backward compatibility.

When both helpers early-exit because of empty bot lists, the loader is
never dereferenced and no DB query fires — the no-bot path stays free.

Includes a regression unit test pinning the dedupe via
`getMessageWithContext.toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`.

Closes #76

feat(im-worker): observe + DLQ ClawHiveService.sendInput failures (#77)

The im-worker post-broadcast fan-out marks the outbox `completed`
before sendInput resolves (sendInput is fire-and-forget — see
post-broadcast.service.ts and issue #77 for the trade-off). A failed
send was previously only visible as a single WARN log line, leaving a
silent observability gap when hive delivery degraded.

This commit closes that gap with two complementary signals:

1. **OTEL counter `im.hive.send_failures`** (in `@team9/observability`'s
   `appMetrics`). Tagged with `error_kind`, `agent_id`, and `tenant_id`
   so dashboards / alerts can group failures and page faster on the
   actionable `no_workers` bucket. Buckets: `no_workers`, `timeout`,
   `http_error`, `other`.

2. **Dead-letter table `im_hive_send_failures`** (migration 0052). Upsert
   on `(message_id, bot_id)` increments `retry_count` + refreshes
   `last_seen_at` / `error_kind` / `error_message`, so a flapping
   downstream produces one row per (msg, bot) instead of an unbounded
   stream of duplicates. Stores `agent_id`, `tenant_id`, `session_id`,
   `tracking_channel_id`, and the original `error_message` for replay /
   audit.

The new helper `recordHiveSendFailure` is invoked from the existing
`.catch` and is itself defensive: if either the counter increment or
the DLQ insert throws, the failure is logged at debug and swallowed —
this is an error handler, the outbox is already done, and we never
want an observability write to escape as an unhandled rejection.

Tests: classifies all four error kinds; counter receives the right
attributes; DLQ row is upserted with `retry_count=1` + the right shape;
counter and DLQ throws are swallowed; `pushToHiveBots` integration
asserts the helper is called with the expected (sessionId, scope,
messageId, …) on a sendInput rejection.

Closes #77

chore(database): rebuild drizzle snapshot baseline so db:generate is clean

The repo had partial drizzle snapshot history (only 0033, 0035, 0044,
0047, 0051 existed for migrations through 0052). 0047's `prevId`
pointed at 0051's `id`, which meant drizzle-kit had a chain collision
when generating any new migration: both 0047 and the new snapshot
claimed the same parent. The visible symptom was that `db:generate`
included drift (topic-session, content_ast, workspace_wikis, etc.) on
top of any intended change — see #76 / 8157b1a0 for the prior
work-around of writing migrations by hand.

Fix:

- Generate a fresh `meta/0052_snapshot.json` from the current schema
  (covers everything that migrations 0044-0052 introduced).
- Drop `meta/0047_snapshot.json` and `meta/0051_snapshot.json` —
  both were broken nodes off the canonical chain (regenerated in the
  wrong order at the time, so their prevIds reference snapshots that
  no longer exist or arrived later). Drizzle only diffs against the
  latest snapshot in normal use, so removing them is safe.
- Pin the canonical migration filename `0052_hive_send_failures.sql`
  back into the journal entry (drizzle's auto-generation uses random
  nicknames; we want descriptive tags).
- Add migrations/README.md documenting the chain history and the
  hand-rolled-SQL-plus-keep-the-snapshot pattern, so the next
  contributor doesn't re-discover this the hard way.

Verification:

- `pnpm --filter @team9/database db:generate` →
  `No schema changes, nothing to migrate` (idempotent).
- All im-worker tests still green (62/62 in post-broadcast).
- The hand-written `0052_hive_send_failures.sql` is unchanged (issue #77).

fix(client): unbreak vitest on Node 25 + tsc Debug Failure crash

Two pre-existing-on-dev issues surfaced while wiring up the ahand
Playwright suite. Both have the same shape: a recent Node release
bundled `localStorage` natively, and TS 5.8/5.9 trips over an
overload-resolution bug whose stack trace doesn't name the file.

## vitest

`pnpm --filter @team9/client test` was crashing at
`src/i18n/index.ts:25` with `localStorage.getItem is not a function`.
Root cause: Node 25 exposes `localStorage` as a global, but its methods
are `undefined` until you pass `--localstorage-file=<path>`. The
truthy-check `if (window.localStorage)` walked into a half-built object
and crashed module load before vitest's setup file could swap in jsdom's
storage.

Two fixes that compose:

- `src/i18n/index.ts` — probe `typeof window.localStorage.getItem === "function"`
  before reading. Robust against Node 25 *and* anything else that
  exposes a stub `localStorage`.
- `apps/client/scripts/vitest-run.mjs` — when running on Node ≥25, set
  `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-webstorage` for the spawned vitest, so jsdom owns
  the global. Probes `process.versions.node` first because the flag
  doesn't exist on Node 22 (CI runner) and is rejected with an error.
- `vitest.config.ts` — exclude `tests/**` so vitest doesn't try to
  discover the Playwright spec files (importing `@playwright/test` in a
  jsdom worker crashes module load).
- `package.json` — route `test:watch` through the same wrapper so the
  Node-25 flag handling applies in watch mode too.

## tsc

`pnpm --filter @team9/client typecheck` was crashing inside `tsc` with
`Debug Failure. No error for last overload signature` and no file/line
hint — same crash on TS 5.8.3 and TS 5.9.3. Bisected by include-paths
to four files that all shared the pattern:

```ts
function deriveStatusLabel(... t: (key: string) => string): string {
  return t("disabled");
}
// caller:
const { t } = useTranslation("ahand"); // typed t with i18next-augmented overloads
deriveStatusLabel(status, enabled, t); // ← TS chokes assigning typed t to loose param
```

The i18next module augmentation gives `t()` a giant union of
overloads. TS 5.8/5.9's overload-resolution path crashes when assigning
that to a parameter typed as a plain `(key: string) => string` *and*
the helper's body returns multiple `t(literal)` calls.

Fix the four callers by inverting the helper: it now returns a typed
*key* (literal-union), and the caller does `t(key)` directly. The
typed-key approach also fails the call at compile time if a translation
key is removed, which the previous loose signature would happily allow.

Files touched:
- `src/components/dialog/devices/ThisMacSection.tsx`
- `src/components/layout/MainSidebar.tsx`
- `src/components/layout/contents/devices/OverviewTab.tsx`
- `src/components/wiki/WikiSettingsDialog.tsx`

After this, `tsc --noEmit` no longer crashes — the remaining 62 errors
it now reports are unrelated, pre-existing issues (cross-namespace
`t("common:cancel")` calls, `import.meta.env`/`glob` typing, etc.).
Those are not blocking and not in scope for this fix.

Verified: `pnpm test` (2091 passed), `pnpm test:e2e --project=ahand-mock`
(5 passed / 4 live-only skipped), and `tsc --noEmit` exits with type
errors instead of crashing. CI doesn't currently invoke typecheck so
nothing gates on the residual errors.

`pnpm --filter @team9/client typecheck` now exits clean. CI never ran
this command, so issues that broke type safety crept in and accumulated.

This change reaches across the surface they touched, but every fix is
local: no behaviour changes, runtime stays the same. Categories:

- **i18next cross-namespace `t("common:foo")`** (10): 4 callers used
  `t("common:cancel")`-style strings while their `useTranslation()`
  was scoped to a single namespace. The strings work at runtime but
  the typed overloads reject them. Fix is to declare both namespaces:
  `useTranslation(["channel", "common"])`. Touched dialogs:
  CreateChannelDialog, CreateWorkspaceDialog, DeleteChannelDialog,
  ApplicationDetailContent.

- **Template-literal `t(\`a.${var}.b\`)` rejected** (4): two distinct
  patterns. Where the variable is a small literal union (OverviewTab's
  systemPerms keys), narrowing the variable's type lets the template
  collapse to a known i18n key. Where the variable is a runtime cross-
  product not enumerated in the typed surface (PermissionsTab's
  group×option keys, PropertySchemaManager's nativeLabels), cast
  through `as never` to opt out of TFunction overload checking.

- **`Promise<unknown>` from `http.get(...)`** (9): ahand-api.ts and
  im.ts called `http.get(...)` without the type parameter, so the
  response chain returned `unknown`. Add `<ResponseShape>` to the
  client method calls.

  Added `aiAutoFillPrompt`, `isRequired`, `defaultValue`,

  `encoding`, `isActive`.

- **`useParams({ strict: false })` returning `never`** (3): TanStack
  Router widens to `never` when no route in the tree declares the
  param. Cast the result to a permissive shape (`{ filter?: string }`
  / `{ channelId?: string }`).

   documents the contract.

  2. SHA bumped without re-vendoring.

Behavioural drift (gateway DTO drifts from schema even when both
files are upstream-synced) is still caught by the existing
`hub-webhook.contract.e2e-spec.ts` round-trip cases. README

fix(gateway/im): extract text from Lexical code-highlight and tab nodes

astToPlaintext's walk() only handled text/mention/linebreak. Lexical's
CodeHighlightNode (type: "code-highlight", inside `code` blocks) and
TabNode (type: "tab") are TextNode subclasses with a `text` field and
no children. They fell through to the "recurse children" branch and
their text was silently dropped.

Impact: clients that paste code or use the composer's code block button
produced a contentAst that translated to an empty `content` string in
messages.controller. determineMessageType still inferred 'text', and
im-worker's gRPC createMessage rejected it with INVALID_ARGUMENT →
HTTP 500 on POST /api/v1/im/channels/:id/messages.

Fix: treat 'code-highlight' and 'tab' as text-like nodes in walk().
Matches Lexical's own $getTextContent semantics. Preserves existing
linebreak and block-separator behavior, so a code block now round-trips
its inner lines joined by explicit linebreaks and ends with a trailing
newline like any block.

feat(tauri/ahand): add browser_runtime commands (status/install/set_enabled) + progress adapter + log tee

Phase C Task 14 of the ahand browser-runtime install/self-check plan.

Adds the Tauri command surface that wires the renderer's "我的设备 →
浏览器控制" UI to ahandd's `browser_setup` library:

- `browser_status` (read-only): inspects all browser components +
  reads `[browser].enabled` from the on-disk config + checks daemon
  online state, returns a unified `BrowserStatus`.
- `browser_install`: runs `browser_setup::run_all`, streams
  `BrowserProgressEvent`s on a `Channel`, tees every raw
  `ProgressEvent` to `~/.ahand/logs/browser-setup-{ts}.log`, and on
  success flips `[browser].enabled = true` + calls
  `AhandRuntime::reload()` so the live daemon picks up the new flag.
- `browser_set_enabled`: short path — flips the config flag and
  reloads, emitting only `Reload*` progress events.

Concurrency: a process-wide `AtomicBool` (`INSTALL_IN_PROGRESS`) gates
mutating commands. RAII `InstallGuard` clears the flag on every exit
path; a second concurrent invocation returns
`Err("operation_in_progress")` synchronously.

Adapter: translates ahandd `ProgressEvent` (with phases
Starting/Downloading/Installing/Verifying/Done/Log) into Tauri-side
`BrowserProgressEvent`s (StepStarted / StepLog / StepFinished /
AllFinished / Reload*). `StepFinished` is emitted via a
reconciliation pass after `run_all` returns — `Phase::Done` fires on
both success AND failure paths in ahandd's `wrap_failure`, so it
cannot be used to drive `StepFinished` directly.

Log tee uses `std::sync::Mutex` (NOT `tokio::sync::Mutex`) — the sync
`Fn(ProgressEvent)` callback runs on the daemon worker thread and
must never call `blocking_lock()` inside a tokio runtime. Logs are
pruned (>7 days) at the start of each install.

Also adds `AhandRuntime::config_path()` accessor used by all three
commands to resolve the on-disk config from the active session.

stdout forwarding, no-stream-drop), `overall_from_reports` priority
(Failed > Ok > NotRun), `StepError.code` snake-case serialization,

fix(ahand): wire AppHandle through reload so daemon-status events reach renderer

Resolves the TODO(task-14) markers left in runtime.rs. Without this,
`reload()` (called by browser_install/browser_set_enabled) respawns
the daemon but the new daemon's `subscribe_status` watcher is fed to
a no-op forwarder (`tokio::spawn(async {})`). Net effect: the
renderer's `useAhandLocalStatus` keeps showing whatever state was
seen *before* the reload, so `BrowserStatus.agentVisible`
(captured the moment browser_install resolves — when the new daemon
is still mid-handshake) never gets a chance to flip true.

Concretely the user observed: install completed cleanly, [browser]
.enabled = true was persisted, but the "Agent 可以使用" Switch kept
its "守护进程尚未应用此设置" out-of-sync warning indefinitely
because no daemon-status update ever reached the front-end after
the reload.

Fix:
- `AhandRuntime`: new `cached_app_handle: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<AppHandle>>>`
  field. Populated on every `start()` (cheap clone). `app_emitter_for_session()`
  now returns the cached handle; reload-spawned daemons get a real
  status forwarder that emits `ahand-daemon-status` like start() does.
- `useBrowserRuntime`: subscribe to `ahand-daemon-status` (same channel
  `useAhandLocalStatus` listens on) and call `refresh()` whenever the
  daemon transitions to "online". Skipped while a command is in flight
  to avoid racing `installDone`/`setEnabledDone`.

fix(im-worker): keep dist flat + add missing @jest/globals devDep

The @team9/storage paths entry in im-worker tsconfig pointed at the
index.ts file instead of the src directory. tsc then treated storage
as a direct input, pushed rootDir up to apps/server/, and emitted
nested dist/apps/im-worker/src/main.js — so the container's
`node dist/main.js` crash-looped with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Aligned the
mapping with gateway/task-worker (../../libs/storage/src) so dist
stays flat.

post-broadcast.service.spec.ts imports from @jest/globals but the
package wasn't declared in im-worker devDependencies, so pnpm strict
isolation left no symlink — tsserver and `pnpm test` both broke for
im-worker.

fix(storage): sign presigned URLs with public endpoint

When S3_PUBLIC_URL differs from S3_ENDPOINT (e.g. internal MinIO
endpoint vs externally reachable URL), presigned download URLs were
signed against the internal host and unusable from clients. Build a
dedicated presign client bound to S3_PUBLIC_URL when the two differ,
and route createPresignedDownload through it. Falls back to the
shared S3 client when only S3_ENDPOINT is set, preserving local dev.

docs(skills-spec): add per-skill agentAccess permission axis

Introduces a 3-state agentAccess enum on skills ('none' | 'read' | 'write')
controlling agent visibility/load/write per skill. Hidden ('none') skills
are filtered out of /v1/bot/skills entirely so search_skills cannot find
them. 'read' allows load + read mounts but blocks write mounts; 'write'
allows everything.

agent-created (the agent owns its own skill).

Enforcement is centralized through resolveSkillAgentAccess(skillId,
botUserId) so the future per-agent-override (v2 §9) can slot in without
changing call sites. Adds a UI control on SkillDetailPage and threads
agentAccess through DTOs, types, and tests.

navigates to /channels/$channelId, which was hardcoded to the workspace
sub-sidebar and forced the Home dashboard into task mode. Clicking an
agent from the Home tab therefore snapped the left rail over to the
workspace / task list instead of staying put.

  activeSidebar, so a channel opened from Home keeps the Home sidebar
  and nav highlight; workspace channels keep the workspace sidebar.
- TasksSubSidebar: treat /channels routes as conversation mode so the
  AI Agents list stays visible, and pass selectedChannelId so the open
  conversation highlights and auto-expands.
- Add regression tests for both behaviors.
